archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (goaltending-sunk)
archetype.definition: A Buffalo team that wins its share of 5-on-5 play but is being buried by the league's worst save percentage and broken special teams, so its results trail its process.

report.headline: Sabres drive play well enough; the goaltending and special teams are sinking them.
report.take:
Buffalo comes off a 109-point season, a fifth-place site ranking and seven playoff wins. Eleven games into 2026-27 it sits at 4-4-3, listed last in the Atlantic and 26th of 32 on the site. Read the standings alone and this looks like a hangover. The 5-on-5 numbers say otherwise. The Sabres own a .511 xGF % (16th) and a .530 CF % (9th). That is a slightly better even-strength profile than last year's .500 and .49. The team that pushed the puck around last spring is still doing it.

What changed is everything around 5-on-5. The goalies have a combined .866 save percentage, 32nd of 32 and well below the league's .892. Goalies GSAx sits at -3.9, and the goaltending grade is an F. Special teams add to the damage: a 10.5% power play (31st) and a 69.2% penalty kill (27th), both about ten points under league average. Together they produce an all-situations PDO of 97.3, 31st in the league, and a goal differential of -10. The defense also ranks 31st in points allowed to forwards above their expected output. That reads less like a coverage collapse than pucks going in at a rate shot quality doesn't explain.

The numbers also hide some luck running the other way. Buffalo's 1.7 Pts vs Goal Diff ranks 2nd in the league. A heavy diet of overtime games has kept the record at .500-ish when the goal differential argues for worse. History helps here. Last year's run came with a 102 PDO and +24.5 GSAx on a roster that was only even at 5-on-5. This franchise's goaltending has swung from +25.5 to -9.5 to +24.5 GSAx in three seasons. The truth is probably between last spring and this October. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (.866, -3.6 GSAx in 8 starts) has to be closer to average for this to turn.

The skater group has a clear shape. The blueline grades B+, led by Owen Power at 27 minutes a night, plus strong xGF shares from Power, Olen Zellweger and Rasmus Dahlin. The forwards grade D+: a productive top group of Jack Quinn, Tage Thompson, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson in front of a center depth chart (McLeod, Norris, Krebs, Helenius) that is all below a 50% xGF share. Benson has a .651 xGF % and no goals on 21 shots, a number that will not hold. The direction is up, but it depends on the crease more than anything else.

strengths.title: Still winning the 5-on-5 game
strengths.body: Buffalo is above water on both expected goals and shot attempts at even strength. The latter ranks inside the top ten. The top line's shares are strong: Benson at .651 and Quinn at .592. This is the most repeatable part of a team's profile, and it is better than last year's, so it should hold.

strengths.title: A blueline that carries minutes
strengths.body: The defense grades B+, and Power is logging 27 minutes a game with a .548 xGF share. Dahlin, who has played 8 of the 11 games, and Zellweger also drive play. Shots against per game are middle of the pack, so the defense isn't the reason goals are going in.

strengths.title: Top-six scoring is there
strengths.body: Quinn (6 goals, 11 points) and Thompson (5 goals on a team-high 45 shots) are producing. Benson's zero goals on strong underlying numbers is a finishing drought, not a role problem. Team shooting % is only slightly below the league, so there's room for the offense to tick up.

concerns.title: League-worst save percentage
concerns.body: A .866 team save % is last in the league, and the goaltending grades an F. Luukkonen carries most of the starts with a -3.6 GSAx. Colten Ellis has a similar save % but a +0.2 GSAx on tougher looks. Some of this will regress toward average, but this franchise's goaltending history is volatile enough that it can't be assumed.

concerns.title: Special teams are broken both ways
concerns.body: The power play converts 10.5% and the penalty kill stops 69.2%, both bottom-six in the league. Last year's PK was 81.9%, so the kill has fallen hard. Part of that is the same goaltending problem, but the power play's 31st rank is its own issue.

concerns.title: The record is ahead of the goals
concerns.body: A 2nd-ranked Pts vs Goal Diff means overtime has propped up the standings. The differential stands at -10 after 11 games. Even with better goaltending, the overtime cushion is the part least likely to repeat.

trend.note: The last five games went 1-1-3 for a .500 points percentage, right in line with the season. The differential is only marginally better than the full-season rate. No turn yet in either direction.

weekAhead.headline: California trip against three outshot teams is a chance to reset
weekAhead.body:
Buffalo heads west for San Jose, Anaheim and Los Angeles. All three sit below 50% in xGF %, and none ranks above 21st on the site. On process the Sabres should carry the play in all three games. The question, as it has been all month, is whether the saves and special teams let that show up on the scoreboard.

San Jose is the trap. The Sharks are badly outchanced at .417 xGF %, but their goalies rank 4th in GSAx and their 26.8% power play is 6th, which is exactly where Buffalo is weakest. Anaheim barely shoots (23.5 shots a game, 29th) but finishes at a high rate. Los Angeles, at 2-5-2 with an F blueline and a 65.5% penalty kill, is the best chance for Buffalo's power play to finally get going. Anything less than two wins on this trip would be a missed opportunity.

keyMatchups.title: Sabres PK vs Sharks power play
keyMatchups.body: San Jose's power play ranks 6th while Buffalo's kill ranks 27th, so penalties are the Sharks' clearest route to stealing a game they'll likely be outshot in. Their A- goaltending can cover the rest. Staying out of the box matters more than usual here.

keyMatchups.title: Buffalo PP gets the Kings' PK
keyMatchups.body: LA's 65.5% penalty kill is 31st, and its blueline grades F. If the Sabres' 31st-ranked power play is going to show signs of life, this is the matchup.

keyMatchups.title: Low-volume Ducks test the goalie
keyMatchups.body: Anaheim takes few shots but converts at a top-ten shooting %. A low-event game puts every save under a spotlight. It is a fair read on whether Buffalo's netminding is stabilizing.

weekAhead.watch: Buffalo's team save percentage on the trip: against three teams that get outshot, competent goaltending should turn possession into wins.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace of 82 points undersells this roster. The 5-on-5 game is sound, the blueline is good, and a .866 save percentage is not a sustainable baseline for any NHL team. As the goaltending drifts toward league norms and the penalty kill follows, the goal differential should move toward even, and Buffalo should climb into the playoff picture. The counterweight is the overtime luck already banked, which won't keep coming at this rate. Last year's 109 points also leaned on a 102 PDO this group probably won't repeat.

The realistic range is a bubble-to-playoff team in the high 80s to mid 90s in points. Goals against should improve from here as the save rate recovers. The upside case needs Luukkonen to look like his better seasons and the power play to climb out of the bottom tier. The downside is that the crease simply stays below average.
swingFactors: Luukkonen's save percentage returning to average
Penalty kill recovering toward last year's level
Benson and the depth centers converting chances

confidence.note: Only 11 games, but the gap between strong 5-on-5 shares and last-place goaltending is large and clear.
